title: Kaempferol-derived carbon dots as antiviral nanomodulators of TLR4 signalling and redox homeostasis in African swine fever virus infection.
authors: Mu, Shuai; Liu, Jia; He, Youhua; Mao, Ruoqing; Ru, Yi; Liu, Huanan; Tian, Hong; Yang, Yi; Zhang, Haixia; Zheng, Haixue; Zhu, Zixiang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山奈酚碳点对非洲猪瘟病毒的抗病毒机制，涉及TLR4信号通路和氧化还原调节，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) offer an attractive platform for engineering bioactive nanomaterials, yet converting small natural molecules into antiviral carbon nanostructures with defined nano-bio functions remains underexplored. Here, we report a solvothermal transformation of kaempferol into water-dispersible carbon dots (KPL-CDs) and investigate how this nanoscale conversion reshapes antiviral activity against African swine fever virus (ASFV). Relative to the parent molecule, KPL-CDs exhibit improved aqueous dispersibility, enhanced biocompatibility, and reduced cytotoxicity in primary porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs). Functionally, KPL-CDs suppress ASFV replication in a dose-dependent manner, accompanied by reduced viral titres, decreased viral particle abundance, and downregulation of ASFV p72 protein and B646L mRNA, the latter encoding p72. Mechanistically, proteomic and biochemical analyses identify the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88)/nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB) axis as a key host pathway responsive to KPL-CD treatment. KPL-CDs attenuate ASFV-induced inflammatory signalling, reduce TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, and IL-18 expression, and simultaneously scavenge intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), indicating coupled regulation of inflammatory and redox homeostasis. Molecular docking and biophysical analyses further support direct interaction between KPL-CDs and TLR4, suggesting receptor-level modulation at the nano-bio interface. These findings show that nanoscale transformation of a bioactive flavonoid can generate emergent antiviral function and identify KPL-CDs as a functional carbon nanomaterial for host-directed control of ASFV infection.
abstract_zh: 碳点（CDs）为工程化生物活性纳米材料提供了一个有吸引力的平台，然而将小分子天然产物转化为具有明确纳米-生物功能的抗病毒碳纳米结构仍未被充分探索。在此，我们报道了山柰酚经溶剂热转化为水分散性碳点（KPL-CDs），并研究了这种纳米尺度转化如何重塑针对非洲猪瘟病毒（ASFV）的抗病毒活性。相对于母体分子，KPL-CDs在原代猪肺泡巨噬细胞（PAMs）中表现出改善的水分散性、增强的生物相容性和降低的细胞毒性。功能上，KPL-CDs以剂量依赖性方式抑制ASFV复制，伴随病毒滴度降低、病毒颗粒丰度减少，以及ASFV p72蛋白和B646L mRNA（后者编码p72）的下调。机制上，蛋白质组学和生物化学分析确定Toll样受体4（TLR4）/髓样分化初级反应88（MyD88）/核因子-κB（NF-κB）轴为响应KPL-CD处理的关键宿主通路。KPL-CDs减弱ASFV诱导的炎症信号，降低TNF-α、IL-1β、IL-6和IL-18表达，同时清除细胞内活性氧（ROS），表明炎症和氧化还原稳态的耦合调控。分子对接和生物物理分析进一步支持KPL-CDs与TLR4之间的直接相互作用，提示在纳米-生物界面上的受体水平调节。这些发现表明，生物活性黄酮类化合物的纳米尺度转化可产生涌现的抗病毒功能，并将KPL-CDs确定为用于宿主导向控制ASFV感染的功能性碳纳米材料。
